evidence_summary: NAMM identifies Bob Seidman as a music wholesaler/distributor, while Tone Machines identifies LIMMCO as the Hicksville, New York wholesale company connected to Nomad, Kimberly, Applied, UMI, Guild and Goya. This supports treating LIMMCO as a commercial network node rather than a universal physical builder.

Tone Machines reports that Bob Seidman said the Kimberly Buzz Box was initially made in the LIMMCO warehouse on Long Island before resource demands led to a third-party builder. The initial manufacturing claim is preserved as period-owner testimony, separate from later supplier states.

A May 1967 Music Trades advertisement is reported by Tone Machines as promoting a new improved circuit design. The available evidence supports a production transition but does not independently name the contract factory in the advertisement record currently reviewed.

The Nomad Super Fuzz resembles an early germanium Mosrite Fuzzrite and is documented as a real Nomad-branded production state, but no model-specific evidence currently establishes a Mosrite, Applied Audio or LIMMCO factory transaction. Nomad therefore cannot inherit the later Applied relationship for this model.

relationship_type: Applied Audio OEM / LIMMCO house-brand distribution
evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies Nomad as a LIMMCO house brand and the Nomad Banshee Fuzz as an Applied Audio product. Manufacturing dates remain uncertain, so the supplier relationship is kept model-specific and provisional.

relationship_type: Applied Audio OEM / LIMMCO house-brand distribution
evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies the Rogue Fuzz as another Applied Audio product available under the Nomad brand. This reinforces the model-specific split inside the Nomad label.
Effects Database catalogs a Nomad Tone Booster as Nomad by UMI. The record supports a UMI-linked product state but does not establish that UMI manufactured the entire Nomad brand range.

Gracin's Music is documented as a music dealer and early UMI customer. Its appearance on multiple pedal supply chains means the Gracin's label should not be treated as evidence of one physical factory.
